Context/Background:
Intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs),  including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasms (IOPNs), and intraductal tubulopapillary neoplasms (ITPNs), are clinically detectable macroscopic non-invasive cyst-forming lesions, some of which progress to invasive pancreatic cancer. Proteins and glycoproteins have proven to be useful clinical biomarkers for classifying cyst-forming neoplasms in the pancreas.Here, we used proteomics and glycoproteomics to characterize a series of histologically and genetically well-characterized surgically resected IPNs, including IPMNs and IOPNs.

Our analysis included 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 macro-dissected grossly normal duct tissues (NDs, with 32 of the 76 NDs coming from the same resection specimens as the IPNs), and 32 cyst fluid samples (22 from matched IPMN patients, 3 matched IOPN patients, 2 from unrelated IPMN patients, and 5 other cysts).
Prompt: Look at the differential genes between high and low grade IPMN and between high grade IPMN and ND. From the commonly upregulated proteins, nominate a few important genes that are related to Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the literature.
output_text:
Introduction/Context
- This analysis employs proteomics/glycoproteomics-derived differential protein data for intraductal papillary neoplasms (IPNs) from Wang 2025 (Cancer Cell, TableS2M). The dataset includes 69 IPNs (64 IPMNs and 5 IOPNs), 76 grossly normal duct tissues (NDs), and 32 cyst fluids. Differential signals were computed for: (i) high-grade IPMN (HG IPMN) vs low-grade IPMN (LG IPMN), and (ii) HG IPMN vs ND. The table provides Uniprot identifiers, gene symbols, and two contrasts: HG vs LG IPMN (with FDR) and HG IPMN vs ND (with FDR).
- From the consistently upregulated proteins (positive HG vs LG IPMN and positive HG IPMN vs ND with FDR < 0.05 for both contrasts), several genes stand out as PDAC-relevant candidates based on their known roles in pancreatic cancer biology (cell cycle, metabolism, adhesion, and growth signaling). Representative examples in the provided subset include TACSTD2 (EpCAM), CDH17, MCM3, MCM7, SLC1A5, SLC3A2, TFRC, and TFF3, among others, each showing robust upregulation in HG IPMN relative to LG IPMN and relative to ND.

Keywords
- IPMN, high-grade IPMN (HG IPMN), low-grade IPMN (LG IPMN), ND (normal duct), PDAC, proteomics, glycoproteomics, TableS2M, differential expression, HG vs LG IPMN, HG IPMN vs ND, cyst fluids, biomarkers.

Candidate Genes
- TACSTD2 (EpCAM)
- CDH17
- MCM3
- MCM7
- SLC1A5
- SLC3A2
- TFRC
- TFF3

Pathway Enrichments (interpretive note)
- The dataset provided does not include explicit, per-library pathway-enrichment outputs (no counts_by_database or top-term tables were supplied in TableS2M). Therefore, formal KEGG/GO term enrichment tables and a computed up/down ratio across databases are not available here. The following results are therefore based on direct gene-level differential signals observed in HG IPMN vs LG IPMN and HG IPMN vs ND, focusing on biologically plausible PDAC‑related processes suggested by the gene set we observe (cell cycle, metabolism, adhesion).

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset
- The commonly upregulated proteins in HG IPMN relative to both LG IPMN and ND include several genes with recognized links to PDAC biology, notably:
  - EpCAM (TACSTD2): a cell‑surface adhesion molecule often elevated in PDAC; associated with epithelial phenotype and tumor progression.
  - CDH17: a cadherin involved in cell–cell adhesion; linked to mucinous/pancreatic ductal lineage contexts.
  - MCM3 and MCM7: replication licensing factors; upregulation reflects enhanced proliferative capacity typical of higher-grade lesions.
  - SLC1A5 and SLC3A2: amino acid transporters; their upregulation aligns with metabolic reprogramming (glutamine uptake and amino acid transport) observed in PDAC metabolism.
  - TFRC: transferrin receptor; frequently upregulated in proliferating cancer cells, including PDAC.
  - TFF3: trefoil factor; associated with mucinous/ductal epithelial biology and potentially IPMN mucinous phenotypes.
- These genes appear in the HG IPMN vs LG IPMN and HG IPMN vs ND contrasts with FDRs < 0.05, and all show positive fold changes in HG IPMN relative to both comparators, consistent with a phenotype shift toward more proliferative, metabolically active, and epithelial-adherent states.

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)

Upregulated (common across HG IPMN vs LG IPMN and HG IPMN vs ND)
| Gene | Direction | Role/Function | Pathway(s) |
| TACSTD2 | Up | Epithelial cell adhesion molecule; cell–cell adhesion at the surface | Cell adhesion molecules; epithelial integrity; PDAC epithelial biology |
| CDH17 | Up | Cadherin involved in mucosal/ductal adhesion | Adherens junctions; epithelial cell adhesion; pancreatic ductal lineage |
| MCM3 | Up | DNA replication licensing factor; drives cell cycle progression | DNA replication; cell cycle control |
| MCM7 | Up | DNA replication licensing factor; partner of MCM2–7 complex | DNA replication; cell cycle control |
| SLC1A5 | Up | Glutamine transporter; supports amino acid uptake | Amino acid transport; metabolic reprogramming (glutamine utilization) |
| SLC3A2 | Up | 4F2 heavy chain; essential for amino acid transport; partners in transporter complexes | Amino acid transport; metabolic adaptability |
| TFRC | Up | Transferrin receptor; drives cellular iron uptake | Iron metabolism; proliferation signaling |
| TFF3 | Up | Trefoil factor; mucin-associated peptide; epithelial/mucosal biology | Mucinous/ductal epithelial biology; barrier/repair pathways |

Downregulated
| Gene | Direction | Role/Function | Pathway(s) |
| Not observed | Down | Not observed as common downregulated in both HG IPMN vs LG IPMN and HG IPMN vs ND in the provided subset | Not available in this dataset excerpt |

Note: The dataset portion shown (60 rows preview from TableS2M) primarily reveals upregulated genes (positive HG vs LG IPMN and positive HG IPMN vs ND) for a number of entries; a formal list of downregulated genes common to both contrasts is not evident in the provided excerpt.

Comparison: overlaps vs tissue-specific
- The majority of the clearly upregulated genes in HG IPMN are consistent across both comparisons, supporting a model in which high-grade IPMN displays augmented proliferative and metabolic programs relative to both LG IPMN and normal duct tissue. The lack of clearly observed common downregulated genes in the shown subset reduces confidence in claims about downregulated programs from this data slice. This pattern suggests a tissue- and grade-associated shift toward replication licensing, amino acid transport, and epithelial adhesion phenotypes in HG IPMN, with potential relevance to progression toward PDAC.

Implications
- The concurrent upregulation of cell-cycle drivers (MCM3, MCM7), metabolic transporters (SLC1A5, SLC3A2), iron uptake (TFRC), and epithelial adhesion markers (TACSTD2, CDH17) in HG IPMN relative to LG IPMN and ND aligns with PDAC-relevant biology (proliferation, metabolic rewiring, epithelial-marker expression). These signals may reflect early PDAC-associated transformation in a subset of IPMNs and support the exploration of these markers as biomarkers for higher-risk IPMNs or early PDAC detection in cyst fluid or tissue.

Next Steps & Clarification
- Validate top PDAC-relevant candidates (e.g., TACSTD2, CDH17, MCM3, MCM7, SLC1A5, SLC3A2) in independent IPMN cohorts and across additional IPMN subtypes (IPMN vs IOPN).
- Perform orthogonal assays (immunohistochemistry on FFPE IPMN sections; targeted proteomics) to confirm upregulation and assess correlation with histologic grade and progression risk.
- Investigate whether these markers are detectable in cyst fluids and whether they can discriminate HG IPMN from ND or LG IPMN in fluid-based assays.
- Integrate these markers with clinical features (grade, dysplasia, cyst size) to build a risk-stratification panel for progression toward PDAC.

References
- Not provided here; PMIDs would be added if explicit enrichment pathways or literature-backed connections were validated in follow-up steps.
